investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod was stuck Unschedulable for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message) confirms that the two nodes capable of hosting PeerPods VMs have no remaining VM slots, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence, causing a complete contract validation failure (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, confirming the agent creation call never completed

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=150156, evidenceKeys=[] — runtime check also failed for the same reason

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior stuck/leaked agent pod consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pod.

Secondary — a prior stuck remote agent pod (consistent with the recent commit message '574b6b2 fix(remote-agents): stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents') may have held VM slots without releasing them, reducing available capacity to zero.
Tertiary — the cluster has only 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm label and the per-node VM quota is too small for the current workload plus eval probes running concurrently.

Quaternary — node affinity or selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only those 2 kata-capable nodes, so even if other nodes had capacity they could not be used; a misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could amplify the exhaustion impact.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain unscheduled for ~143–148 seconds before the eval timed out. Because no agent pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned an agent, and the remote-agent-state probe could not collect any of its four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), producing a complete contract gap.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes. No preemption victims were available, and the four remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck in Unschedulable state for the full ~143–148 s observation window, preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the remote-agent-state probe to reach the state-polling step or emit any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the two eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes, and no preemption victims exist, indicating all VM slots are occupied by existing workloads or leaked pods.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the pod's node affinity or nodeSelector targets only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are at capacity — a configuration or capacity-planning issue rather than a scheduler bug.

Leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if previous eval cleanup (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs) failed to delete pods, those pods would continue to consume VM quota and starve new scheduling attempts.

Cluster under-provisioned for concurrent remote-agent eval load: if multiple eval runs or production workloads compete for the same 2 kata-capable nodes simultaneously, transient exhaustion is expected without capacity scaling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Failing: Kubernetes Kata PeerPods VM Resource Exhaustion on Production Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are fully allocated, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. The pod was stuck Unschedulable for ~148 seconds before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence and failing every required contract assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message) confirms that the two nodes capable of hosting PeerPods VMs have no remaining VM slots, and preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner received no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence, causing a complete contract validation failure (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior stuck/leaked agent pod consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for the eval probe pod.

Secondary — a prior stuck remote agent pod (consistent with the recent commit message '574b6b2 fix(remote-agents): stop polling state of dead/stuck remote agents') may have held VM slots without releasing them, reducing available capacity to zero.
Tertiary — the cluster has only 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm label and the per-node VM quota is too small for the current workload plus eval probes running concurrently.

Quaternary — node affinity or selector on the remote agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only those 2 kata-capable nodes, so even if other nodes had capacity they could not be used; a misconfigured or overly restrictive affinity rule could amplify the exhaustion impact.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes have no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 nodes did not match pod affinity/selector), causing every remote agent pod to remain unscheduled for ~143–148 seconds before the eval timed out. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes. No preemption victims were available, and the four remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck in Unschedulable state for the full ~143–148 s observation window, preventing agent creation and making it impossible for the remote-agent-state probe to reach the state-polling step or emit any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote-agent pods, so even if VM capacity were freed, only 2 nodes are eligible. A misconfiguration or recent node pool change could have reduced the eligible node count.

Tertiary — a cluster scaling or autoscaler delay: the cluster may be configured to scale out kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes on demand but the scale-out did not complete within the eval's observation window (~143s), causing the scheduler to report Unschedulable before new capacity arrived.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or the cluster resource dashboard shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unused on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and a pod spec misconfiguration or API-level rejection would need to be investigated instead.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all five required evidence fields, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike or autoscaler lag) rather than a sustained capacity exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have been recently relabeled or had their affinity configuration changed to exclude remote-agent pods, the primary cause would shift from VM capacity exhaustion to node affinity misconfiguration.

If the remote-agent pod spec was recently changed to request more kata.peerpods.io/vm units per pod (increasing per-pod demand), and the cluster capacity was not adjusted, the root cause would be a resource-request change rather than organic capacity exhaustion — this would require reviewing the pod spec diff, which is not present in the supplied evidence.

If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with scheduling errors, the problem may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource type; if local checks are passing, the failure is isolated to the remote/kata.peerpods.io/vm scheduling path.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the Kubernetes scheduler or cluster resource API for kata.peerpods.io/vm slot availability and alerts when free capacity drops below a configurable threshold — this would catch capacity exhaustion before it causes pod scheduling failures.
Add a check that monitors the count and age of stuck/unscheduled remote-agent pods in the cluster, alerting when any pod remains Unschedulable for more than a configurable duration (e.g., 60s).

Add a check that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity selector meets a minimum threshold, catching node pool shrinkage or label drift before it reduces scheduling capacity.

Consider a canary eval that attempts to schedule a minimal remote-agent pod on a short interval (e.g., every 5 minutes) and reports scheduling latency, so capacity pressure is visible as a trend before it becomes a hard failure.
